title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a Babylonian and went up to the Land of Israel, as in Ketubot 112b: when he came to the border of the Land of Israel he rolled in its dust (out of his great love for the Land of Israel). There he received from all the great men of the generation, as we find “Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said that Rabbi Yose ben Shaul said” in Rosh Hashanah 24a and 30a, Moed Katan 22a and Ketubot 104a. Hyman suggests that perhaps what was said in Megillah 31b, “From where do we derive that one does not interrupt? Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said that Rabbi Assi said: For the verse says, ‘My son, do not despise the Lord’s discipline,’” is Rabbi Yose ben Shaul, who is sometimes called Rabbi Assi ben Shaul, as in Shabbat 50a. Dikdukei Soferim reads “Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said that Rabbi Simai said,” and Hyman prefers this reading. In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:8 the statement reads: “One does not interrupt in the curses. Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said: ‘Do not loathe His reproof’ — do not make it into pieces.”

Likewise Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, as in Sotah 7a; and he said, “It was thrown from the mouth of the group,” Shabbat 3a and Pesachim 64a, and Tosafot on Shabbat there explain: a group of Tannaim. Hyman finds some slight support from this for the inference that he went up to the Land of Israel in Rav’s time, when there were still groups of the last Tannaim.

notes.text: Hyman’s Assi/Yose ben Shaul/Simai alternatives remain competing proposals; his inference from the last Tannaim is only slight, as supplied. קוצים קוצים is rendered in pieces, retaining the pun without invented literal thorns in the curses reading.

The inspected Megillah 31b directly reads Assi; Shabbat 50a directly names Assi ben Shaul. Neither establishes Hyman’s proposed equivalence with Yose ben Shaul or verifies the precise Dikdukei Soferim Simai reading. Shabbat 3a and Tosafot directly give the group-of-Tannaim explanation, with Tosafot also recording an alternative explanation. Hyman’s migration inference remains only slight; Ketubot 112b directly gives the dust-rolling act.
